candidateAudit.title: 🇦🇹 We went to Vienna. Naturally, we ate our way through it. Somewhere between the grand cafés, Christmas markets and long walks through the city, we found ourselves doing what we
candidateAudit.text: 🇦🇹 We went to Vienna. Naturally, we ate our way through it. Somewhere between the grand cafés, Christmas markets and long walks through the city, we found ourselves doing what we always do: discovering a place through its food. And Vienna certainly knows a thing or two about good food. Here's what made it onto our plates: 🍟 Fries with truffle mayo — Golden, crispy, generously dipped in truffle mayo. Not particularly Austrian, but we weren't about to say no. 🌭 Käsekrainer — A smoky, juicy sausage with little pockets of melted cheese. Best eaten standing outside, preferably when it's freezing. 🥞 Kaiserschmarrn — Fluffy pancakes torn into pieces, caramelised in butter and buried under icing sugar. Served with plum compote. Messy in the best possible way. 🥘 Saftgulasch — Beef slowly cooked in a rich onion and paprika gravy. The sort of dish that makes you forget how cold it is outside. 🥩 Tafelspitz — Tender boiled beef, aromatic broth and a few traditional sauces. Understated, comforting and deeply Viennese. 🍋 Wiener Schnitzel — Thin, golden, impossibly crisp. A squeeze of lemon, and really, what more do you need? 🍫 Sachertorte — Chocolate, apricot jam and more chocolate. A little piece of Viennese history, served with whipped cream. 🍰 Gewürzgugelhupf — A softly spiced, ring-shaped cake that feels like something someone's grandmother would make on a Sunday afternoon. 🍎 Apfelstrudel — Paper-thin pastry, warm apples, cinnamon and raisins. Proof that some recipes don't need reinventing. What we loved most wasn't just the food itself. It was how much of Vienna's history still lives in these recipes.
